p0_archive.rule: Every archived leg reads only pinned Git objects through the manifest of native_creation_binding.py, assembled with the working tree closed. It runs only archive code: the 24bfb6a helpers it copies, which tests compare with their Git objects, and the archive's own loader, assemblies, phases and checks. It compiles and runs its JVMs in its own work directory without an inherited class path, and is checked against frozen expectations and the pinned 24bfb6a predictions. The source checks refuse any archive function or archive data that uses a living name. So living code and the current sources do not change its inputs or results; only an edit of the archive itself does.
p0_archive.labels: Living runs carry production or legacy, archived runs rollback-reader or archived-baseline. Every Format.V1 read by the current sources is legacy: the version gate and future format tests, the last manager case, the b1-v1 reader and its rollback check, and the V1 reader cases of b1 focused and its mutants. In this runner rollback-reader labels only the pinned 24bf-v1 and 7845 readers and their rollback checks; the history and counter admission runners also give it to the Format.V1 runs of the archived 24bfb6a parity side.

p7_guard_reading.status: PREDICTED before the guarded run of P7 candidate f. Nothing here is an executed result.
p7_guard_reading.basis: Every rule of the production format guard reads the compiler's translation of unicode escapes (javac's UnicodeReader rules: Character.digit digits, several u and the backslash before an escape) through one lexical view of comments, literals and text blocks that ends a line comment at a CR or LF. The escape rule refuses every backslash followed by u in a production text. A store construction is read in every syntactic form, in a structure view where literal contents and annotations (balanced, nested ones included) are blank: explicit type arguments, type annotations and qualification, and a constructor reference with type arguments. Code outside printable ASCII is refused, so names compare exactly. Native sources also refuse method and constructor lookup by name. The two escape mutants hide a V1 store construction behind an escaped line break, so the site and format rules now see it too; a harmless escape trips the escape rule alone, and neither fullwidth escape digits nor an escaped carriage return hide anything.
